title: Knockout and gap-filling
summary: Removing unmatched or conflicting terms can produce a contract governed partly by the Code’s supplied terms.
notes: C. Itoh’s subsection (3) contract includes agreed terms plus applicable supplementary provisions; its rejected arbitration clause cannot return as a gap-filler. Northrop’s knockout of different terms in a subsection (1) setting is a separate interpretive issue. The similar practical result should not obscure the distinct statutory routes. The notes ask whether Code defaults are neutral and how those defaults shape drafting incentives.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 281–294. Open assigned page 281.
